# Test fixtures

Small CSV files for tests. Each covers a case the CSV loader must handle.

| File | Case |
|---|---|
| `simple.csv` | Comma separator, header, three numeric columns (40 rows) |
| `semicolon_decimal_comma.csv` | European style: `;` separator, `,` as the decimal mark |
| `tabs.csv` | Tab separator in a `.csv` file |
| `dates.csv` | ISO dates (`2026-01-01`) as the x column, two series for overlays/bars |
| `datetimes.csv` | ISO date-times (`2026-10-21T08:15:00`) |
| `missing_and_comments.csv` | `#` comment lines, quoted header with spaces, empty cells, `NaN` |
| `run_a.csv`, `run_b.csv` | Same columns in two files, for overlay (`+`) tests |
| `text_categories.csv` | Text x column (month names), for bar charts |
| `scaling.csv` | Values over five decades, for log–log axes |
| `decay.csv` | Exponential decay, for a log y axis |
| `samples.csv` | 60 measurements in three sites with error columns, for hist, box, error bars and fits |
| `matrix.csv` | A correlation-style table with row names and an empty first header cell, for heatmaps |
| `surface.csv` | x, y, z on a 25×25 grid (long form), for contours and heatmaps |
| `grid.csv` | The same kind of surface as a table: header = x, first column = y |
| `pattern.csv` | Angle (degrees) and gain, for polar plots |
| `messy.csv` | Three junk lines above the header, two 999 glitches, two blanks: `skiplines=`, `clip=`, `dropna` |
| `workbook.xlsx` | Two sheets: `Run1` (with an Excel date column) and `Run2` (two junk rows above the header) |
| `readings.json` | An array of objects (rows), with a text column |
| `series.csv` | x and ten gently wavy series `s1`…`s10`, one above the other: every point shape |
| `signal.csv` | 1000 samples at 1 kHz: `voltage` = 50 Hz (size 1) + 120 Hz (size 0.5) + noise, `current` = 50 Hz (size 0.3): `fft` |
| `heating.csv` | A made-up heating scan: `storage` steps down near 105 °C, `loss` peaks near 100 °C, `damping` is their ratio: `peaks`, `onset`, `area=`, `slope`, `cross=` |
| `trial.csv` | A made-up plant trial: `growth` and `yield` (each with sd) against `dose`, two very different ranges: twin axes, `values`, `corr`, `fitlabel=` |

| `garden.csv` | A made-up garden in long form: `bed` (Shade / Part sun / Full sun), `soil` (Clay / Loam, some with a leading space), `width`, `depth`, `yield` with `yield_sd`, `mass`: `by=`, `groups=`, `strip`, `highlight=` |
| `effects.csv` | Seven made-up factors and their share of the variation in `height` and `flowers`, one row each: horizontal bars, `highlight=`, `values=%.0f%` |
| `spectrum.csv` | A made-up spectrum: two peaks (100 at 50, 40 at 72) on a curved baseline 20 + 0.15x + 0.0008x², a little noise; `clean` = the peaks alone: `baseline=`, `showbaseline`, `norm=area` (7) |
| `outlier.csv` | Six samples, four near 12–15 and two near 480–495: a broken axis (`ybreak=20:460`) (8b) |
| `formats.csv` | Five readings one hour apart (06:00–10:00 UTC) written in four time zones (`+02:00`, `Z`, `+01:00`, `-05:00`), amounts with thousands marks (`"1,234.5"`): shown on the Mac's clock, read as numbers (10) |
| `runs/` | A folder of three short runs (`day1`…`day3`, columns `t`, `temp`): a folder in place of a file gives one panel per file (10) |

Large files for speed checks are generated by the tests, not committed.
